subject: Phylo.integration function - summary gives an r-PLS of 1?

messages.author: 364b34b2b0ded261
messages.subject: Phylo.integration function - summary gives an r-PLS of 1?
parts:
Hi all

It's me again, I'm sorry.

I performed a 2B-PLS analysis in a phylogenetic context using "phylo.integration(X, Y, phy)". Both X and Y contain shape data (one for the triquetrum and one for the ulna), and the summary of the analysis gives me a r-PLS=1 (and a p=0.001), which means than all my points are aligned on a perfect diagonal. This is a strange result, as the regular 2B-PLS analysis shows some covariation between the shape of both bones but no perfect alignment (which is the case when phylogeny is taken into account).

I came across a similar message from 2 years ago, and there the problem was a 'bug' in the phylo.integration function. However, I'm now using the newest version of R and I updates all the packages so I don't know what is going on here?

Thanks!

Marie.

Marie,

 

The function works fine, as per example below (a simple example where the result is not r.pls = 1.0). Check to see that you are providing it inputs correctly.


Dean

 

data(plethspecies)

Y.gpa<-gpagen(plethspecies$land)    #GPA-alignment

land.gps<-c("A","A","A","A","A","B","B","B","B","B","B")

 

phylo.integration(Y.gpa$coords,partition.gp=land.gps,phy=plethspecies$phy)
